Alex — great questions, thanks for writing them up. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps before your Friday architecture review:

Recap / short answers:
- Chat vs completions: Use chat endpoints when you need multi-turn state, system/instruction tokens, or function/tool calling (structured output). Use completions for single-turn prompts where you control framing and don't need tool-calls.
- Tokenization / max_tokens: Start with a conservative max_tokens for responses (e.g., 512) and validate against your transcript sizes. We can provide a token-encoding script; recommended approach is to truncate oldest context when you hit limits and consider selective summarization for long histories.
- Streaming + structured output: Streaming is supported; when you expect structured JSON/tool-calls, we recommend emitting a final non-streamed commit event (or a deterministic closing token) to validate structure. Dev will add notes below.

Attachments: attaching a short request/response schema proposal and the SDK quickstart. See attached rsp-schema-proposal.json and redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf.

Proposed next steps:
1) Dev to send a short note with SDK auth examples and examples for tool-calling and embeddings/rerankers.
2) We can run a 30-min tech deep-dive with your infra team Thursday (10/21) or Friday (10/22) — please confirm availability.
3) If you want, we can produce a sample tokenization run on one of your redacted transcripts — send a small sample.

Thanks,

Hi Alex — adding a few technical clarifications and short examples to help your infra/eng review:

SDK / auth:
- Redwood SDKs (Python/Node) support API key and OAuth flows; for Private/Dedicated we support mTLS and token exchange via your IdP. Example header: Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_KEY>.
- Quickstart in the attached PDF shows environment variables and a one-file example to call chat streams.

Chat vs Completions (example):
- Chat (multi-turn + tools): send messages = [{"role":"system","content":"you are a response generator"}, {"role":"user","content":"..."}] and enable function_calls for tool/vector database lookups.
- Completions (single prompt): send prompt string. There is less opinionated structure and fewer built-in tool hooks.

Tokenization / max_tokens:
- Use our token-encoder lib (included in SDK) to compute token usage before sending. We'll return usage in response headers to help you bill/play nice with limits. For long transcripts we recommend: 1) drop or summarize non-critical turns, 2) offload embeddings of long documents and rerank top candidates for context, 3) use incremental summarization to keep context small.

Streaming + structured output:
- Streaming will emit partial chunks. If you rely on valid JSON, either: 1) stream only plain text and produce structured JSON at the end, or 2) use function-calls which return structured payloads in a final event. We also support a delta/commit model where the final commit provides checksum/validation.

Embeddings / rerankers:
- Recommended pattern: precompute embeddings for your doc corpus, at query time embed the user query, retrieve top-K, then pass the small context into chat/completions for final generation or a ranker model for scoring. We can share sample code.

Let me know what language your team prefers and I can paste a short SDK snippet.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
